question: Why does DAG-L/L drop from 52.5% (Mono-L) to 31.5% on TAT-QA 200? Which layer contributes most: extraction error, interface information loss, reasoning degradation, or execution/parser failure?

B_current_dag.description: Current DAG-L/L: large extraction → large reasoning → deterministic execution (existing frozen result)

C_full_context.description: DAG with full-context passthrough: extraction stays, but reasoning ALSO sees the complete original context alongside extracted facts
C_full_context.tests: interface information loss (does the facts-only interface lose context needed for reasoning?)

D_gold_facts.description: DAG with gold facts: extraction output replaced with gold literals from the task derivation; reasoning and execution unchanged
D_gold_facts.tests: extraction error (are upstream extraction mistakes the bottleneck?)

metrics: Harm recovery count (how many of the 56 B-failures does each version fix?)

interpretation.C_recovers: interface information loss is the main bottleneck → improve interface representation
interpretation.D_recovers_but_C_doesnt: extraction error is the main bottleneck → improve extraction node
interpretation.neither_recovers: decomposition-induced reasoning degradation → reconsider decomposition granularity
interpretation.expression_correct_but_answer_wrong: execution/parser loss → fix deterministic execution interface

hard_rules: same 200 tasks as frozen decomposition benchmark
same model pool, generation config, scorer
extraction responses reused from frozen B (no new extraction calls)
gold facts derived from task derivation using same literals() function as original benchmark construction
reasoning prompt format follows frozen sprompt with modification only for C (add context) or D (replace facts)
